opportunities.title: Go device SDK: Parakeet readiness races with PCM submission
opportunities.summary: On main `7163538913e15dd86534b41dc695e2a5639c0774`, normal PCM submission during a Parakeet connection's ready handshake triggers a Go data race: `NewParakeet`'s reader goroutine writes `wsTranscriber.ready` at `sdks/device/go/omidevice/stt/stt.go:131`, while `AppendPCM` reads it at line 44 without synchronization. I reproduced this through the public constructor and `AppendPCM`, using real HTTP/WebSocket framing over `net.Pipe` with synthetic audio and no network service, hardware, or real credentials. The regression fails under `go test -race` before the fix. Replacing the flag with `atomic.Bool` preserves the pre-ready gate and immediate Deepgram readiness; the complete Go suite passes 20 race-enabled runs, `go vet` passes, and the repository preflight passes all 119 selected checks. The test also rejects a deliberately broken early-ready gate within five seconds, and the patch received an independent code review. This report establishes the data race; it does not claim an observed production outage or lost transcript. The tested patch and regression are ready on [the fix branch](https://github.com/projectnaseem/omi/tree/fix/go-stt-ready-state). @josancamon19, would you approve

opportunities.title: Developer API PATCH ignores explicit null when clearing an action item's due date
opportunities.summary: **Product impact** - Primary loop layer: Retrieval-Action. - Developer API clients cannot remove an action item's due date using the documented PATCH contract. A stale due date can also leave the corresponding reminder scheduled. **Describe the bug** At commit `7163538913e15dd86534b41dc695e2a5639c0774`, the developer action-item PATCH route documents `due_at: null` as removing the due date, but only includes `due_at` in the update when `request.due_at is not None`. **To reproduce** Given an existing unlocked action item `a1` with a due date, send either request to `PATCH /v1/dev/user/action-items/a1`: ```json {"due_at": null} ``` ```json {"description": "Updated task", "due_at": null} ``` **Current behavior** The first request returns 422 (`At least one field must be provided`). The second succeeds but retains the old due date. These results were reproduced in a local, isolated FastAPI TestClient harness; I have not tested your deployed service. **Expected behavior** Explicit `null` clears the date and reconciles the existing reminder. Omitting `due_at` preserves the date; a non-null valid date replaces it. **Verification and scope** A focused patch and 10 regression cases are prep

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
